title: Housing: the funding question that never gets answered
note: The brand sheet's own example, run as a TV panel. A deflection, a question dodged twice, an ad hominem, a moderator's natural transition, a nod, and a cue.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Good evening and welcome. Tonight we start with housing, and the government's promise of new homes.

turns.speaker: MIN
turns.text: Our plan builds 40,000 homes by 2028, fully funded.

turns.speaker: SHD
turns.text: How is it funded? You haven't said.

turns.speaker: MIN
turns.text: What I can tell you is that crime is up under your government.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Minister, the question was about funding. Where does the money for the homes come from?

turns.speaker: MIN
turns.text: We have committed record investment and we are getting on with the job.

turns.speaker: SHD
turns.text: Record investment, from a man who has never built a shed, let alone a house.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Let's leave it there and turn to immigration. Shadow minister, your party says it would cut net migration.

turns.speaker: SHD
turns.text: We would bring net migration down to 300,000 a year.

turns.speaker: SHD
turns.text: And we would do it by clearing the asylum backlog first.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Hepta, anything to flag so far?
